summary.plain: A beam of neutrinos sent 732 kilometres straight through the Earth's crust, from CERN in Switzerland to the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy, between 2006 and 2012, so that the OPERA experiment could watch them change type on the way.
summary.technical: CERN Super Proton Synchrotron protons directed onto a graphite target to produce a muon-neutrino beam aimed 732 km through the Earth's crust at LNGS; operated July 2006 to December 2012, providing the neutrino source for the OPERA experiment's νμ → ντ appearance search.

target.quote: a beam of protons from the Super Proton Synchrotron at CERN
target.value: Graphite target struck by SPS protons, producing pions/kaons decaying to muons and muon neutrinos
